label: input k/p/w at original position 2 after particular first-two-token contexts (e.g. j e)
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (0.03% of steps). Almost all activations (95% of activations and 96% of mass) are on input k, p or w (k > p >> w) early in the sequence: original position 2 (58% of mass), position 3 (17%), or the first copy step after <DEL>, where k/p is re-fed as orig(0) (23%). On its own that token/position gate is very imprecise (precision about 1%), so whether the unit fires depends on which tokens came just before. It is strongest when the two preceding tokens come from {j,h,e,1,f} (two back) and {z,e,0,t,f,c,r,j,h} (one back). j as the first token is the strongest context (e.g. j e k). That reads like an additive token-weight conjunction rather than one clean rule. The recorded predicate covers only the position-2 case, so it misses position 3 and the copy-step firings (e.g. k h f <DEL> k, which is the max activation). Never fires at t=0,1, at the delimiter, or on letters other than k/p/w (a few a/m/d/l only). Magnitude is highest for k, for prev2=j, and for the copy-step k/p after short sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: in_tok=k (+4.94), in_tok=p (+4.88), L=3 & recall_idx=1 (+3.67), prev2_tok=j (+2.91), prev2_tok=e (+2.90), prev_tok=z (+2.69). Lower it: in_first=0 (-2.09), recall_idx=4 (-1.54).
